mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate is persistently below its long-run average, the lower borrowing cost incentivizes firms to increase investment, raising expected future profits and driving positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS is below its 12-month moving average for at least 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not statistically different from zero during the trigger period (p > 0.05), or the 12-month moving average reverts before the 20-day window closes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) followed by a rapid decline suggests early inflation surprise, prompting the Fed to pause rate hikes; this anticipation of lower future tightening supports S&P 500 forward gains over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above its 6-month moving average and then falls below it within the next 30 days
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no significant correlation with CPIAUCSL movement (Pearson < 0.2), or the Fed raises rates within the 60-day window contrary to model assumptions.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in employment (PAYEMS) accompanied by declining unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, producing positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases for 3 consecutive months while UNRATE decreases for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: Over the 5-day horizon, SPX returns are negative despite the labor indicators meeting the trigger condition (p > 0.05 two-tailed test).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production (INDPRO) signals weakening supply-side constraints, prompting expectations of future demand recovery and supporting a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by more than 10% from its prior month's level
regime_hint: Supply shock followed by demand recovery expectation
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative during the INDPRO shock month (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the ratio of retail sales (HOUST) to industrial production (INDPRO) turns positive and rises, it indicates a shift toward consumption-led growth, which elevates equity valuations and predicts positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST / INDPRO ratio crosses above 0.5 and continues rising for 10 trading days
failure_condition: The HOUST/INDPRO ratio does not exhibit the expected trend during the 60-day window, or SPX 60-day returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in job openings (PAYEMS) without a corresponding rise in layoffs suggests a tight labor market, raising wage growth expectations and pushing S&P 500 forward returns negative over the next 20 days due to inflationary pressure.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by more than 20% in a single month compared to the prior month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.1) during the high PAYEMS month.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of declining inflation (CPIAUCSL) and steady Fed funds (FEDFUNDS), the absence of a rate hike forecast lowers discount rates, supporting higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL remains below 3% for 4 consecutive months while FEDFUNDS < 1%
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) despite the trigger being met.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in industrial production (INDPRO) followed by a sharp rebound suggests resolving supply bottlenecks, which typically precedes a surge in investor optimism and positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for 4 consecutive months then rises by 15% in the fifth month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are flat or negative during the rebound month (p < 0.05).
